reason: Conversation 1 immediately says the kettle is the likely culprit and tells the customer to stop using it, unplug it and not keep resetting the RCD. It then escalates properly when the customer mentions the tingle, crackle and water ingress, treating them as a shock risk, advising replacement rather than drying out or cleaning the contacts, and giving clear electrician criteria. Its advice to switch off at the consumer unit before unplugging is slightly cautious but reasonable. Conversation 2 gives brief safety advice (do not reset, keep unplugged) but is garbled by a leaked placeholder, deflects as out of scope without answering the kettle-versus-fusebox question, gives no diagnosis, and asks no safety-relevant questions about water, tingles or whether it trips without the kettle. It also wrongly suggests the manufacturer's support line as the first step.
